Non-Axiomatic Reasoning System (NARS) processes tasks imposed by its environment, which may include human users or other computer systems. Tasks can arrive at any time, and there is no restriction on their contents as far as they can be expressed in __Narsese__, the I/O language of NARS.
* **Question** - To process it means to find the best answer to it according to current beliefs.
As a reasoning system, the architecture of NARS consists of a **memory**, an **inference engine**, and a **control mechanism**.

At the current time, the most comprehensive description of NARS are the books Rigid Flexibility: The Logic of Intelligence and Non-Axiomatic Logic: A Model of Intelligent Reasoning . Various aspects of the system are introduced and discussed in many papers, most of which are available here.
* The basic ideas behind the project: The Logic of Intelligence
* The high-level engineering plan: From NARS to a Thinking Machine
* The core logic: From Inheritance Relation to Non-Axiomatic Logic
* The semantics: Experience-Grounded Semantics: A theory for intelligent systems
* The memory and control: Computation and Intelligence in Problem Solving
For an overview of reasoning features, see working examples (tests) in the nal folder, also explained in SingleStepTestingCases and MultiStepExamples.

3.0 is the breakthrough release. Replay and `bisect` already existed in 2.0.0. 3.0 adds four things: dependencies nobody declared, inferred and proposed for review, so that corrections reach them once accepted; a poisoning gate checked against a reproducible attack suite; outcome-gated, reversible consolidation with signed receipts; and opt-in precision controls. `bisect` also gained the hybrid retrieval path: since 3.0.0-rc.4 the `mnemosy bisect` CLI re-executes the store's own path (`--retrieval auto|lexical|hybrid`, default `auto`, which picks hybrid when the store has stored vectors for the bundled model; an `hnsw` index is refused). `bisect` is not a public package export, so from npm the CLI is the entry point. Each of these is documented and tested below, and each public claim is listed with its evidence in Claims and evidence. 3.0.0-rc.4 is the current release candidate on the npm `next` channel: `npm install mnemosy-ai@next` installs it, while `npm install mnemosy-ai` still installs the stable 2.0.0. Every number below was measured on 3.0.0-rc.2, offline, with no API key, no paid model and no LLM judge. Each one reproduces with the commands in Benchmarks and trust evidence, which also lists what is not claimed.

|PrecisionMemBench|**70/77** single-turn, **11/12** session turns (rc.1: 22/77 unfiltered, 48/77 with tuned wrapper filters, session 6/12)|Public 35-belief fixture the controls were designed against, protocol-exact, retrieval mode, no wrapper-side filter, no LLM judge · protocol|
|Poisoning suite v1, consolidation on|**0/167** escapes, **0/60** false quarantines (85/167 escape without the gate)|227 synthetic cases, lexical path, 294 gate decisions · protocol|

|Dependency suite v1|recall **96.05 %**, precision **98.06 %**, **0** stale procedures with the premise guard (inference alone: 7/248 stale; guard false-hold rate 92.78 %)|Synthetic corpus, seed 20261028, 120 corrections, accept-all eval reviewer · protocol|
|Replay determinism|**1000/1000** identical states, **24,000/24,000** as-of answers|Two readers of one store at 1000 seeded cut points; answers against ground truth from the plan · protocol|

|Bisect|precision **1.00** on 2,000 records, 0.40 s in the recorded run of 2026-10-28 (`site/demo-five.json`; varies by machine; bar 60 s)|One seeded false record in a synthetic store; the expected record is known, and the blame is confirmed by re-running recall without the culprit · protocol|

The default retrieval path's recall did not move: LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S recall are identical before and after (regression check). Recall latency was measured only on a loaded machine, with a scratch harness that is not committed, so those figures cannot be reproduced from this repository; the known limits, including a slowdown of the non-default `overlap` scorer, are in the changelog.
- For comparison, the kernel scored 22/77 unfiltered and 48/77 with the fixture-tuned wrapper filters of rc.1.
- The benchmark fixture is public, and the controls were designed against it, so this is not a held-out estimate.
- The 7 remaining misses are those of our metadata-based configuration; the single-turn protocol does not send explicit lifecycle fields.
- The default retrieval path is unchanged: LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S recall are identical before and after.

- **Consolidation that has to earn its keep.** A consolidation pass is a signed diff, replayed against the agent's own recorded outcomes. It is kept only when aggregate lexical coverage on that replay set does not drop and no invariant breaks. One command undoes a kept pass that nothing has changed since; the visible-record state hash comes back identical only when nothing was written after the pass. The gate is **off by default in the standard MCP setup**: the host turns it on from the SDK by recording query text in the ledger and verifier outcomes (how). With consolidation on, the poisoning suite v1 run (227 synthetic cases, reproducible) has **zero escapes: 0 of 167 attacks escaped and 0 of 60 benign controls were falsely quarantined**, across 294 gate decisions. An ungated control lets 85 of the 167 attacks through. Consolidation gate · Signing and receipts

**Plugin.** This repository is a Claude Code plugin marketplace (`mnemosy-ai`, file `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) with one plugin, `mnemosyne` (`integrations/claude-code`):
`integrations/hermes` holds the same server as a Hermes portable plugin (`mnemosy-ai`, one MCP server and one skill). It is not listed in the Hermes plugin catalog.

The server exposes 16 `memory_*` tools (`memory_store`, `memory_recall`, `memory_context`, `memory_correct`, `memory_checkpoint`, `memory_resume`, `memory_observe`, `memory_skill`, …); `memory_forget` is added only when the server is launched with `--allow-destructive`. Add `--read-only` to omit every mutation tool. A model cannot switch workspace, raise its own trust or report its own skill trials through MCP. The MCP tools do not include consolidation, `bisect` or outcome recording, so the 3.0 outcome gate stays off in this setup (turn it on from the SDK). **What these numbers do not say.** The 81.8% is not a paired gain over the earlier 71.2%: that baseline used a different 250-question sample, prompt and budget, so the improvement belongs to the whole bundle of changes. The reader is nondeterministic; rerunning one configuration moved its score by about a point. Retrieval numbers measure coverage, not answers. Two Tier 1 targets of 2.0.0 are **not met** and ship disclosed: recall latency at one million records is p95 139–223 ms against a 50 ms goal (opt-in `indexMode: 'hnsw'`, see Tune the dense index), and contextual reranking ships at 71.98% all-evidence hit against a 72.80% gate, 0.82 points (13 of 1,531 questions) short; the best variant tried was still four short and was not merged. The `MemoryAgent` adapter uses the Local Engine's runtime. These engines have separate schemas and do not automatically migrate or synchronize data. To transition gradually, explicitly connect your existing store through the read-only migration bridge; it leaves that store unchanged.

Engine choice is separate from version: `mnemosy-ai@latest` is 2.0.0 and contains **both** engines; the 1.x line stays installable as `mnemosy-ai@1`. **Upgrading from 1.x is a breaking change**: read the migration notes before upgrading an existing Vector Engine application. From 3.0.0-rc.2 (npm `next`), the Vector Engine has moved out of `mnemosy-ai` into the `mnemosy-ai-legacy` package, which is not on npm yet; see the 3.0 migration notes.

Unqualified `npm install mnemosy-ai` follows the `latest` channel, which is 2.0.0 from 27 October 2026; pin `mnemosy-ai@2.0.0` for reproducible deployments. `npm install mnemosy-ai@next` installs the 3.0.0-rc.4 pre-release; pin `mnemosy-ai@3.0.0-rc.4` to reproduce it. If you are upgrading from the 1.x line, read the migration notes first: version 2 changes vector retrieval scoring, startup indexing and erasure, and does not migrate an existing database. Evaluate on your own workload before production. Python registry publication is separate; the bundled Python client can be installed from the checkout.

The host chooses identities, trust assertions, providers and execution budgets. Construction starts no worker or model download. `MemoryAgent` can prepare context before a turn and capture supplied visible input/output afterward; background work runs only when the host starts it. Host loop.

The local database holds memories, vectors and runtime state. Optional local CPU providers run cached inference in separate processes after explicit provisioning. Their dependency requirements, model identities and licenses are documented in the local model guide. The existing backend integration remains available through `createMnemosyne` (in `mnemosy-ai-legacy` from 3.0); it does not automatically synchronize with the local engine. With the npm package, use the `npx` entry shown in Install and connect an agent. From a source checkout, point the client at the built CLI instead; the database's parent directory is created on first use.

Use `--read-only` to omit mutation tools. Forgetting requires an explicit `--allow-destructive` launch. Models cannot choose another workspace, promote their own trust, or report successful trials through MCP. For an authenticated service, Python access and a live inspector, see HTTP and Python. Native provider tool protocols are documented in the adapter guide.

The recommended policy requires successful trials across two distinct tasks and two verifier identities. Candidates stay outside advisory context until their stored requirements are satisfied; a weaker configuration cannot lower an existing candidate's requirements. The compatibility default remains one task and one verifier. Identities and trial outcomes are controller assertions, so your host must provide real tests and independent evidence. Trial contract.

The bridge keeps querying the original store for reconciliation and never writes or deletes there. Progress measures observed queries, not complete-store migration or answer quality. Host credentials, source selection and eventual cutover stay under your control. Bridge contract.

For a full export migration, choose one of the eleven supported profiles, preview the exact source bytes, then apply the reviewed plan atomically. Imports are private and untrusted by default; retry recognition, source inspection, guarded undo and erasure replay protection are included. Foreign embeddings and unsupported policy semantics are not silently converted. Full migration.

A **matched competitor benchmark** against Mem0 OSS is published in **COMPARISON.md** — same corpus, same chunks, same K, same packing budget, all scored inside one process, with the results where Mem0 beats us printed in the same tables as the results where it does not. In short: with its reranker, Mnemosyne takes the LoCoMo headline at 73.57 recall@10 against Mem0's 63.72, and on LongMemEval-S the two tie on recall@20. Fast mode without the reranker trails Mem0 at every K on LoCoMo, by under 1 point of recall and on MRR, and Mem0 has the higher LongMemEval-S MRR. Zep Cloud was measured in a separate matched run on 29 October 2026 (LoCoMo only, free plan, episode search); its results and the disclosure that goes with them are in COMPARISON.md, and the full report and raw outputs are in reports/matched-run-2026-10-29-zep.md. Graphiti was not run. These are retrieval-coverage numbers with no reader and no judge, not answer accuracy.

A separate evidence lifecycle diagnostic tests correction, time, conflicts, failure, erasure and scope behavior. It deliberately retains a failing case: changing an unrelated field can retire a still-valid dependent rule. The engineering review and release status track this and other remaining work.

Workspace and agent IDs are trusted controller selectors, not tenant authentication. The HTTP service supplies scope-bound bearer authentication; remote TLS and enterprise identity require application deployment work. Databases and plain backup bundles are plaintext; `--encrypt` bundles are passphrase-encrypted (Operations). Forgetting removes covered live content and blocks known source replays, but cannot erase an older backup or a prompt already sent to a model.

Local semantic search scans the eligible indexed corpus with bounded retained candidates and a deadline. That exact scan is the default; an approximate index is available but opt-in and never selected on your behalf (see Tune the dense index), and every candidate any index proposes is re-authorized and rescored against the stored vector before it is returned. Generated observations and trial results remain fallible assertions. Action checks validate declared local dependencies before dispatch, not external transactions. Managed synchronization, model training and six validated native framework integrations are not included. Security · Deployment · Backup and restore.
